title: Envelope vs Mint: Which Budgeting App Wins in 2026?
summary: Mint is gone. See how Envelope compares in our Envelope vs Mint breakdown — and find the proactive budgeting app that stops overspending before it starts.
body_markdown:
[Mint shut down on March 23, 2024](https://www.expensesumo.com/blog/best-mint-alternatives) after 17 years, leaving 3.6 million active users scrambling for a replacement. If you were one of them, you have already lived through the frustration of a budgeting platform disappearing overnight. Now, with fresh options on the market, the real question is whether a proactive, envelope-style app like[Envelope](https://envelopebudgeting.com/) can do what Mint never quite managed: help you stop overspending before it happens, rather than tallying the damage after.


This comparison breaks down what Mint was, why it failed, and how Envelope stacks up as a modern, forward-thinking replacement.


### Key Takeaways


-


**Mint is gone for good:**[Mint, the personal finance app](https://vento.money/blog/mint-shutdown-what-now/) that once had over 20 million users, was officially shut down by Intuit on March 23, 2024, and users were migrated to Credit Karma, which has a fundamentally different purpose, credit monitoring, not expense tracking. Build your budget on a platform with a viable long-term business model.


-


**Reactive vs. proactive design:** YNAB is often described as the philosophical opposite of Mint. Mint showed you where your money went after you spent it, while proactive apps make you assign every dollar a job before you spend it. Envelope follows the same pre-spending philosophy.


-


**Digital envelopes beat tracking-only apps for lasting habits:** According to[envelopebudgeting.com's analysis of digital cash stuffing](https://envelopebudgeting.com/articles/best-envelope-budgeting-app) , digital budgeters maintain their savings rate better at the six-month mark, 68% retention vs. 52%, due to convenience. Choose a method built for the long haul.


-


**Envelope merges budgeting and banking:** Envelope is a budgeting app with a built-in checking account and debit cards, so you can manage your money and stick to your budget all in one place. That structural integration is something Mint could never offer.

### What Mint Was, and Why It Disappeared


#### The Mint Promise


[Mint attracted users with a simple](https://getfinny.app/blog/best-mint-alternatives-2026) promise: connect your bank accounts, and the app handles the rest. It auto-imported transactions, categorized spending, tracked bills, and showed your net worth across all linked accounts, all for free. For many people, it was the first time personal finance felt manageable.


#### The Fatal Business Model


[Mint shut down on March 23, 2024](https://vento.money/blog/mint-shutdown-what-now/) after Intuit announced its closure in late 2023. The app's business model, free in exchange for showing users targeted ads and partner financial product recommendations, collapsed once Apple's App Tracking Transparency and Google's privacy changes broke the ad-tech pipeline that Mint relied on.


The lesson for anyone choosing a budgeting app today: free-with-ads is a fragile model. The features Mint users relied on most, transaction categorization, budget tracking, and spending analysis, either didn't exist in Credit Karma or were significantly reduced. The migration was a downgrade for anyone who used Mint primarily for budgeting or debt tracking.


> **Pro Tip:** When evaluating any budgeting app, check how it makes money. A subscription model, even a modest one, typically signals longer product stability than an ad-supported free tier.


### Envelope: Best Overall Mint Alternative


#### Why Envelope Earns the #1 Spot


Envelope is a budgeting app with a checking account and debit card built in, so you can plan your money, control spending, and budget from one place. That structural combination is something a tracking-only app cannot offer: a system where the budget categories and the actual money live in the same product.


In my experience, the biggest failure point for former Mint users is the gap between where their budget lives and where their money lives. Mint tracked your Bank of America account, but the budget was in Mint, and your money was still at the bank. Envelope closes that gap entirely.


Set your direct deposit to your Envelope account, fill your envelopes on payday, and every debit card purchase draws down the right envelope in real time. The system runs itself after the initial setup, enforcement happens automatically, because the transaction already drew down your envelope balance the moment you paid.


#### Key Features


[Envelope delivers instant](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/envelope-budgeting-banking/id6444296251) transaction notifications for real-time spending awareness, separate virtual and physical cards to organize finances by category, and built-in joint accounts designed to support collaborative budgeting.


[A net worth tracker covers assets](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/envelope-budgeting-banking/id6444296251) and liabilities over time, and a Protected Envelope offers a high-yield savings option to maximize funds set aside for specific goals.


**Pros:**


-

-


Funds are FDIC insured up to $250,000 through Pacific West Bank, Member FDIC


-


Couples get individual logins with shared envelope pools


-


Virtual cards per envelope, when a category runs dry, that card declines automatically


-


Early paycheck access available


-


Competitive high-yield savings rate on protected envelopes


**Cons:**


-


Requires switching your primary checking account, which is a bigger commitment than downloading a tracking app


-


No investment portfolio tracking (Empower handles this better)


-


Smaller user community compared to YNAB or Monarch


### How Mint's Top Alternatives Compare


#### Quicken Simplifi, Best for the Mint Transition


[If you want the closest experience](https://www.financialaha.com/articles/mint-alternatives-after-shutdown/) to what Mint was, Simplifi is probably it. Automatic transaction import, spending categories, and budget tracking, the core features work similarly. At about $48 per year, it is affordable for an app with automatic imports. The tradeoff is that you are still tracking after spending, not controlling before.


#### Monarch Money, Best for Power Users


[Monarch was built by a former Mint](https://www.financialaha.com/articles/mint-alternatives-after-shutdown/) product manager who apparently saw the writing on the wall, and it was literally designed to be what Mint could have become with continued investment.[At $99 per year, it costs more](https://www.financialaha.com/articles/mint-alternatives-after-shutdown/) than Simplifi, but users who have tried both often prefer Monarch's polish and features.


#### Empower, Best Free Option for Investors


Empower provides a net worth and portfolio tracker and is accessible on both mobile and desktop devices. If Mint served you mainly as a net-worth dashboard rather than a category budgeting tool, Empower is the cleanest free path forward.


> **Pro Tip:** I've found that former Mint users fall into two camps: those who used it to track spending (who need Envelope or Simplifi) and those who used it to watch net worth (who need Empower). Identify which camp you belong to before switching; it will save you weeks of trial-and-error.

The behavioral difference here is meaningful.[Research shows people spend 12-18%](https://wealthvieu.com/personal-finance/budgeting/envelope-budgeting/) less when using cash versus cards, and envelope budgeting with virtual cards replicates that psychological limit digitally. That is the discipline Mint's passive tracking model could never deliver.


### Common Mistakes When Switching from Mint


**Mistake 1: Replacing Mint with another tracking-only app.** Tracking after spending is the same habit that let Mint users overspend month after month. The app changed; the behavior did not. Switch to a pre-spending system.


**Mistake 2: Choosing an app based on brand recognition alone.**[Budgeting apps are becoming](https://www.academybank.com/article/banking-trends-in-2025-and-beyond-budgeting-apps-for-financial-success) increasingly popular and used more consistently, nearly 80% of budgeting app users engage with their platforms at least weekly. The most-used app and the most-effective app are rarely the same thing.


**Mistake 3: Ignoring the business model.** Mint failed because advertising revenue dried up.[The biggest shift since Mint's](https://getfinny.app/blog/best-mint-alternatives-2026) shutdown is that free, bank-connected budgeting is no longer the default. A small subscription fee, like Envelope's $40 per year, is what keeps a product funded and improving.


### Frequently Asked Questions


#### Why did Mint shut down?


[Intuit discontinued Mint on March](https://getfinny.app/blog/best-mint-alternatives-2026) 23, 2024, after 17 years. The company chose to consolidate its consumer finance efforts under Credit Karma, another Intuit-owned property. Mint's free model, which relied on financial product referrals and targeted ads, was reportedly no longer sustainable at the scale needed to maintain the service.


#### Is Envelope a direct replacement for Mint?


Envelope and Mint serve related but structurally different purposes. Mint was a free budgeting app that allowed users to create budgets, sync financial accounts for automatic tracking, track their net worth, and manage recurring subscriptions and bills. Envelope goes further by combining those budgeting functions with an actual checking account and debit card, so the budget enforces itself at the point of purchase rather than reporting on damage after the fact.


#### How much does Envelope cost compared to what Mint charged?


[Envelope's pricing](https://envelopebudgeting.com/) starts free and then runs at $4 per month, $40 per year, or a one-time lifetime option. Mint was free, but it shut down.[Envelope costs $40 per year, while](https://envelopebudgeting.com/articles/best-budgeting-apps) YNAB charges $109 per year, yet both deliver powerful results, making Envelope one of the most affordable full-featured options in the category.


#### What happened to Mint user data after the shutdown?


[After the shutdown, migration](https://vento.money/blog/mint-shutdown-what-now/) moved over connected accounts and net-worth tracking, but it did not bring across the budgeting and category-spending features Mint users actually relied on. That data gap is one of the core reasons millions of former Mint users are still looking for a real replacement in 2026.


### The Verdict


Mint was a useful tool for its era, passive, free, and frictionless. Its shutdown revealed the core weakness of that model: a product your bank balance depends on should have a business model that can last.


[Envelope](https://envelopebudgeting.com/) earns the top spot here because it solves the problem Mint never cracked, the gap between where your budget lives and where your money lives. By combining envelope budgeting with a real checking account and Visa debit card, it converts intentions into automatic enforcement. Former Mint users who want genuine spending control, not just a prettier dashboard, will find it the most complete step forward available in 2026.
